skill.description: Create AI avatar, talking head, lip-sync, and dubbing videos with inference.sh belt CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Generate AI presenter and lip-sync videos through guided inference.sh CLI workflows.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline model names, and example CLI commands, not executable Ruby or shell evaluation. The hardcoded URLs are documentation links, image assets, or placeholder media inputs for the intended inference workflow. One semantic marketplace risk remains: the synthetic media workflows need explicit consent, rights, and disclosure guidance.

remediation.issue: Synthetic avatar and dubbing workflows lack consent and disclosure guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear requirements for consent, likeness rights, voice rights, copyright review, and synthetic media disclosure before generation.

remediation.issue: External inference processing may receive user media, scripts, and audio URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note explaining that inputs are processed by inference.sh and selected model providers.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples triggered static command and network detections.
remediation.suggestion: Label command blocks as user-run examples and replace placeholder URLs with clearly marked placeholders where possible.

semantic_findings.title: Synthetic Media Impersonation Safeguards Missing
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises talking head, lip-sync, virtual presenter, and dubbing workflows but does not tell users to verify consent or disclose synthetic media. This can facilitate misleading impersonation if used with a real person's likeness or voice.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The advertised use cases and dubbing workflow are explicit, and no consent, rights, or disclosure guidance appears in SKILL.md. The finding is about misuse potential, not proven malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Producing talking head videos often requires editing tools, voice generation, and model selection. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code CLI workflows for avatar video generation.
actual_capabilities: Runs P-Video-Avatar examples through the inference.sh belt CLI.
Shows model options for P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse Lipsync.
Supports text-to-avatar workflows with built-in text to speech.
Supports avatar videos from portrait and audio URL inputs.
Outlines portrait generation followed by avatar video creation.
Outlines dubbing workflows using transcription, translation, speech generation, and lip sync.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, belt CLI access, and network connectivity.
Model availability, pricing, speed, and output quality can change outside the skill.
Users must provide media URLs and confirm they have rights to each asset.
The skill does not verify consent, likeness rights, copyright, or disclosure requirements.

use_cases.title: Product Presenter Videos
use_cases.description: Create short avatar-led product demos from a portrait and approved script.

use_cases.title: Training Explainers
use_cases.description: Generate consistent talking head lessons for onboarding, support, or course content.

use_cases.title: Localized Video Dubbing
use_cases.description: Plan a workflow to transcribe, translate, voice, and lip-sync existing videos.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Avatar Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow with the recommended model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a 20-second presenter video from my portrait URL and short script. Choose the recommended model and explain expected cost factors.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Voice Audio
prompt_templates.scenario: Avatar video from a portrait and external audio file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking head video from my portrait URL and approved audio URL. Select the best model for lip sync quality.

prompt_templates.title: Build Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a dubbing workflow for my existing video. Include transcription, translation review, speech generation, and final lip sync steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Production Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for quality, cost, and speed tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available avatar models for a campaign with ten short videos. Recommend settings for speed, cost, quality, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: I need a 30-second product demo with a friendly AI presenter.
output: Recommended model: P-Video-Avatar for built-in speech and lower cost.
Inputs needed: approved portrait, final script, voice choice, language, and resolution.
Review step: confirm the likeness, script, and disclosure text before generation.

output_examples.input: I have a portrait and a recorded voiceover for a training video.
output: Suggested workflow: use the portrait and voiceover as direct inputs for lip sync.
Quality checks: clear audio, front-facing portrait, and correct pronunciation.
Risk check: confirm consent for the image and voice before processing.

output_examples.input: I want to localize an existing explainer video into Spanish.
output: Workflow: transcribe the source video, translate the script, generate Spanish speech, then lip-sync the result.
Review step: have a fluent speaker approve the translation and timing.
Disclosure step: label the localized result as AI-assisted when required.

best_practices: Use only portraits, voices, and scripts that are approved for synthetic video generation.
Start with low-cost settings, then raise resolution after the script and timing are final.
Keep scripts concise and review generated videos for lip sync, tone, and disclosure needs.
anti_patterns: Do not create avatars of real people without permission and a clear review process.
Do not include confidential, regulated, or customer-sensitive information in scripts or media URLs.
Do not treat generated videos as final without checking likeness accuracy and rights.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create avatar, talking head, lip-sync, and dubbing videos through inference.sh CLI workflows.

faq.question: Which model should I try first?
faq.answer: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar because it includes text to speech and targets lower cost.

faq.question: Can I use my own voice recording?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes workflows that use an audio URL instead of built-in text to speech.

faq.question: Does the skill create portraits?
faq.answer: It includes an optional workflow that generates a portrait first, then uses it for avatar video.

faq.question: Does it verify media rights?
faq.answer: No. Users must confirm consent, likeness rights, copyright permissions, and disclosure rules.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the inference.sh belt CLI, account access, and network calls to model providers.
